quick_notes.title: Phobias & Manias
quick_notes.detail: Claustrophobia (Enclosed space), Acrophobia (Height), Hydrophobia (Water). Bibliomania (Books), Pyromania (Fire).
quick_notes.explanation: Phobias and manias are two types of extreme or irrational mental states. A phobia is an intense, unreasonable fear of a specific thing or situation, such as Claustrophobia, which is the fear of enclosed spaces like elevators, or Acrophobia, the fear of heights, or Hydrophobia, the fear of water. A mania is an excessive, often uncontrollable enthusiasm or obsession for something, such as Bibliomania, which is an extreme passion for collecting books, or Pyromania, which is an uncontrollable urge to set fires. In simple terms, a phobia makes you terrified of something, while a mania makes you obsessed with it.

quick_notes.title: Types of Government
quick_notes.explanation: A government is the group of people who make and enforce rules for a country. In a democracy, the power to rule comes from the people, usually through voting in elections. An autocracy is the opposite, where one single person, like a dictator or king, holds all the power and does not share it with anyone. A plutocracy is a system where the richest people in society control the government and make decisions to benefit their own wealth. An aristocracy is a form of government run by a small group of noble or high-born families who inherit their positions. Finally, a bureaucracy is a government where power is held by the officials or administrators who work in government departments and follow strict rules and procedures to manage the country.

quick_notes.title: Personality Types
quick_notes.detail: Philanthropist (Loves mankind), Misogynist (Hates women), Altruist (Selfless), Egoist (Self-centered).
quick_notes.explanation: Personality types describe how people think and act toward others. A philanthropist is a person who loves all of humanity and works to help people, like someone who donates money to build schools. A misogynist is someone who hates women, often treating them unfairly or with disrespect. An altruist is a selfless person who puts others' needs before their own, like a volunteer who gives food to the hungry without wanting anything back. An egoist is a self-centered person who only cares about their own needs and feelings, ignoring what others want.

quick_notes.title: Group Names
quick_notes.detail: A flock of sheep, A pride of lions, A herd of cattle, A school of fish, A choir of singers.
quick_notes.explanation: Group names are special words that tell us what to call a collection of the same kind of animal or person. For example, a flock of sheep means many sheep together, and a pride of lions means a group of lions living together. A herd of cattle refers to a large number of cows or bulls moving or grazing as one. A school of fish describes many fish swimming together in coordinated movement. A choir of singers means a group of people who sing together, usually in a performance. So, instead of saying "a group of lions," you say "a pride of lions" because that is the correct collective name.

quick_notes.title: Tricky Spellings
quick_notes.detail: Occurrence, Committee, Millennium, Lieutenant, Questionnaire, Receipt, Privilege, Maintenance.
quick_notes.explanation: The tricky spellings list includes words that are often misspelled because of silent letters, double letters, or unusual letter combinations. In occurrence, remember two c's and two r's: it comes from occur plus ence. Committee has two m's, two t's, and two e's at the end. Millennium has two l's in the middle and two n's at the end. Lieutenant is spelled with i-e-u and a silent t, while questionnaire has a double n after the first e. Receipt has a silent p, privilege ends with e-g-e (not e-d-g-e), and maintenance has an e in the middle after n, not an a.
